ch0_boot.title: Wheel Check
ch0_boot.goal: Drive to all three test beacons.
ch0_boot.hint: Follow the orange light in the distance. The arrow on your screen points to the next beacon.
ch0_boot.success: All systems go. Echo is ready to roll.

targets.name: Beacon 3
targets.found: Antenna is picking up a signal.

ch1_sites.title: Pick a Landing Site
ch1_sites.goal: Scout photos of three areas. Choose the safest place to land in each one.
ch1_sites.hint: Big craters are dangerous, and so are boulders. Choose the patch with the fewest of each.
ch1_sites.success: Good choices. This is the same kind of work that scientists did with Ranger and Surveyor images.
ch1_sites.question: Round {{n}} of {{total}}: which site is safest?
ch1_sites.right: Safest choice: this site has the fewest hazards.
ch1_sites.note: Practice images, generated for this game.

ch1_landing.title: Soft Landing
ch1_landing.goal: Touch down at less than {{safe}} m/s. Hold the thruster to slow your fall.
ch1_landing.hint: Wait for it, then burn. Fire too early and you'll run out of fuel high above the ground.
ch1_landing.success: Touchdown! Much smoother than Surveyor's real two bounces.
ch1_landing.fail_crash: Crash at {{speed}} m/s. Start your burn a little sooner.
ch1_landing.fail_fuel: Out of fuel. Wait longer before you start the burn.

ch2_laser.title: Catch the Light
ch2_laser.goal: Find the Sea of Tranquility near the middle of the Moon and fire the laser at the reflector {{shots}} times.
ch2_laser.hint: Look for the large dark patch just right of the center. The target is close to the equator.
ch2_laser.success: You just measured the distance to the Moon with light.
ch2_laser.instruction: Click or tap the Moon to fire the laser.
ch2_laser.miss: No echo. The pulse didn't hit the reflector.
ch2_laser.drift: Since 1969, the Moon has drifted about {{m}} m farther away.

ch2_lrv.title: Follow the Rover Tracks
ch2_lrv.goal: Visit three geology stops. Stay within walking distance of the lander.
ch2_lrv.hint: The red ring on the radar shows your limit. Apollo crews had the same rule: they had to be able to walk back.

targets.name: Elbow Crater
targets.found: Stop 1: rocks thrown out when an impact formed the crater.

targets.name: Mountain Base
targets.found: Stop 2: ancient rock from the Moon's mountains.

targets.name: Hadley Rille
targets.found: Stop 3: a long channel that was probably carved by lava.

ch3_slingshot.title: Borrow a Planet
ch3_slingshot.goal: Pick the launch day and speed so Jupiter gives your probe at least 1 km/s extra.
ch3_slingshot.hint: Your probe must arrive just after Jupiter passes, behind the planet.
ch3_slingshot.success: Jupiter just threw your probe toward the outer planets, with no fuel needed.
ch3_slingshot.suggested: Mission Control set a good window.
ch3_slingshot.diagram: Orbit diagram with the Sun, Earth, Jupiter, and your probe's path
ch3_slingshot.fail_short: Not enough speed. The probe never got as far as Jupiter. Launch faster.
ch3_slingshot.fail_missed: Too far from Jupiter when you got there. Change Jupiter's starting position.
ch3_slingshot.fail_bound: Close, but the flyby added too little speed. Adjust by a few degrees to pass just behind Jupiter.
ch3_slingshot.fail_hit: Right into Jupiter! A little farther away, please.

ch4_landing.title: Down Through Thin Air
ch4_landing.goal: Open the parachute, then fire your engines. Land at less than {{safe}} m/s.
ch4_landing.hint: Open the parachute right away. Start burning when you are a few hundred meters up.
ch4_landing.success: On the ground! The first successful US landing on Mars happened on 20 July 1976.
ch4_landing.fail_crash: Crash at {{speed}} m/s. Did you open the parachute before burning?
ch4_landing.fail_fuel: Out of fuel. Let the parachute do more work first.

ch4_lr.title: Is Anyone Home?
ch4_lr.goal: Read Viking's soil experiments and decide what they mean.
ch4_lr.hint: Scientists don't jump to conclusions. Look at all three results together.
ch4_lr.success: That's the real answer: strange chemistry and no clear evidence of life.
ch4_lr.note: Charts show the general shape of the results, not the raw data.
ch4_lr.noneLabel: A flat instrument trace with no peaks

rounds.title: Test 1: Fresh soil + nutrients
rounds.q: What happened after the nutrients were added?
options: The soil gave off a burst of gas
rounds.explain: Radioactive gas came out quickly. That could mean something was eating the nutrients.

rounds.title: Test 2: Soil baked first
rounds.q: The heated soil stayed quiet. Why does this matter?
options: Heat stopped the reaction, which is what you'd expect from life or from some chemicals
rounds.explain: Baking changed the result. Living things could explain that, but so could chemicals broken down by heat.

rounds.title: Test 3: Looking for organic molecules
rounds.q: No organic molecules were detected. So what's the best conclusion?
options: Mars is definitely full of microbes
Strange chemistry, no clear evidence of life
rounds.explain: Viking found surprising chemistry, but no clear evidence of life. Scientists are still studying what it means.

ch5_opportunity.title: Follow the Water
ch5_opportunity.goal: Scan all four rock outcrops before the dust storm blots out the sun.
ch5_opportunity.hint: You charge in sunlight and use power when you drive. When the battery is low, stop and wait for the sun.
ch5_opportunity.success: You found the signs of water, just as Opportunity did.
ch5_opportunity.fail_storm: The dust storm has blocked the sun. That's exactly what happened to Opportunity in June 2018.
ch5_opportunity.low: Battery empty. Waiting for the sun.

targets.name: Blueberry Field
targets.found: These small spheres contain hematite, a mineral that usually forms with water.

targets.name: Layered Outcrop
targets.found: Layers like these can be laid down by water.

targets.name: Eagle Crater Rim
targets.found: Impacts expose older rock from below.

targets.name: Endurance Crater
targets.found: Evidence that this place was wet long ago.

ch6_ingenuity.title: Thin Air
ch6_ingenuity.goal: Tap the rotors to hover inside the green band for {{hold}} seconds, then land gently.
ch6_ingenuity.hint: Don't hold it down. Short taps keep you steady.
ch6_ingenuity.success: Powered flight on Mars! Ingenuity did this 72 times.
ch6_ingenuity.fail_crash: Hard landing at {{speed}} m/s. Tap the rotors to slow down near the ground.
ch6_ingenuity.fail_fuel: Battery is flat. Use shorter taps.

ch7_golden.title: Pack the Golden Record
ch7_golden.goal: Which of these are really on the Golden Record? Sort each one.
ch7_golden.hint: It was made in 1977 as a phonograph record, which holds sound and picture data.
ch7_golden.success: You know what we chose to say about ourselves.
ch7_golden.note: The record holds 115 images, greetings in 55 languages, natural sounds, and music from many cultures.

whales.name: The songs of whales
whales.why: Yes. Natural sounds include surf, wind, thunder, birds, and whales.

video.name: A video of a rocket launch
video.why: No. The record carries sounds and images, not video.

greetings.name: Hello in 55 languages
greetings.why: Yes. They run from ancient Akkadian to Wu, a modern Chinese dialect.

thunder.name: The sound of thunder
thunder.why: Yes. Earth's weather made it onto the record.

map.name: A street map of every city
map.why: No. It does show where Earth is, but it has no city maps.

music.name: Music from many cultures
music.why: Yes. Musical selections come from different cultures and eras.

m1_drive.title: Under the banyan tree
m1_drive.goal: Drive the lunar rover to the three markers beneath the old tree. Use the arrow keys, WASD, or the buttons.
m1_drive.hint: The arrow at the top left points to the next marker. Drive slowly over the ridges.
m1_drive.success: The wheels remember the way. Cuội and the rabbit are waiting under the tree.

targets.name: Old tracks
targets.found: Tracks from 1971, still sharp in the dust.

targets.name: The banyan roots
targets.found: Roots stretch across the regolith like roads.

targets.name: The shade of the tree
targets.found: Here the dust is cool. Someone has been sitting here.

m2_collect.title: Four sample sites
m2_collect.goal: Drive to four sites and collect a rock from each. The rover was built to carry samples like these.
m2_collect.hint: The arrow points to the next site. You have no time limit. Look around.
m2_collect.success: Four samples secured. Now let us find out what they are.

targets.name: Dark patch
targets.found: A smooth, dark rock. It looks like cooled lava.

targets.name: Bright slope
targets.found: A pale, chalky rock, lighter than the dust around it.

targets.name: Broken ground
targets.found: A rock made of many pieces stuck together.

targets.name: Small crater rim
targets.found: A rock with a story written in its cracks.

m2_samples.title: Read the rocks
m2_samples.goal: Look at each sample and choose its type. A wrong guess is a clue, not a failure: look again.
m2_samples.hint: Colour and texture are the best clues. Dark and smooth, pale and chalky, or pieces pressed together.
m2_samples.success: You read six samples like a field geologist.
m2_samples.question: Sample {{n}} of {{total}}: which rock is this?

props.basalt: Dark, smooth, and heavy. Formed from cooled lava.
props.anorthosite: Pale and chalky. Part of the Moon's bright highlands.
props.breccia: Many broken pieces pressed together by an impact.

m2_samples.wrong: Not quite. Look at the colour and the texture again.
m2_samples.note: Choose the rock type that matches what you see.

m3_craters.title: Which ground is older?
m3_craters.goal: Compare four patches of the lunar surface. Pick the patch that looks older and more weathered.
m3_craters.hint: Older ground has more craters, softer edges, and fewer sharp boulders.
m3_craters.success: You read the surface like a map of time.
m3_craters.question: Patch {{n}} of {{total}}: which ground has been exposed longer?
m3_craters.right: Yes. More craters and softer edges mean an older surface.
m3_craters.wrong: Look again: count the craters and check how sharp their edges are. The older patch is {{letter}}.

m4_signal.title: Follow the old signal
m4_signal.goal: Drive toward the faint signal. It is older than the rover, and much quieter.
m4_signal.hint: The signal gets stronger as you get closer. Follow the arrow.
m4_signal.success: The signal is coming from a small package half buried in the dust.
